cards.text: It's the first year of Darius son of Xerxes, a Mede, made ruler over the kingdom of the Chaldeans. Daniel, one of God's people living far from Jerusalem, is reading the sacred books, and he comes to the word of the LORD to Jeremiah the prophet about Jerusalem's desolation. Daniel's not skimming, friend. He's doing the MATH.

cards.question: In the word of the LORD to Jeremiah, how long would the desolation of Jerusalem last?
So Daniel turns his attention to the Lord God, to seek Him by prayer and petition. What else does Daniel bring with him?

answers.text: A feast with music and dancing

cards.text: Sackcloth and ashes. Daniel is NOT playing around. I once wore the same floury apron four days straight, but friend, that was laziness, not repentance.
Then Daniel prays, and before he asks for anything, he starts with who God is. The great and awesome God, who keeps His covenant of loving devotion to those who love Him and keep His commandments.

cards.question: When Daniel confesses, he talks about the people's sin but leaves himself out of it.

cards.text: Daniel says WE: we sinned, we did wrong, we acted wickedly, we rebelled. When something goes wrong at work, everybody suddenly gets VERY interested in their phone, but Daniel raises his hand.

cards.question: Daniel says they didn't listen to God's servants the ___, who spoke in His name to their kings, leaders, fathers and all the people.

cards.text: Daniel says righteousness belongs to God, but shame covers the people: the men of Judah, the people of Jerusalem, and all Israel near and far, in every country God drove them to because of their unfaithfulness. Their kings, their leaders and their fathers too.

cards.question: The people are covered with shame. But Daniel says something belongs to God, even though they rebelled against Him. What is it?

cards.text: Daniel keeps going. They didn't obey the voice of the LORD or walk in His laws, so the oath and the curse have been poured out on them.

cards.question: Daniel says the oath and the curse poured out on them were written in the Law of ___.

cards.text: Daniel says God has carried out the words spoken against them by bringing a great disaster. Under all of heaven, nothing has ever been done like what's been done to Jerusalem.

cards.question: After all that disaster, Daniel says the people turned from their iniquities and sought the favor of the LORD.
Daniel says the LORD brought the calamity on them, and that the LORD is righteous in all He does.
Daniel reminds God how He brought His people out of the land of ___ with a mighty hand.

cards.text: Now Daniel asks. He prays that God's anger and wrath would turn away from His city Jerusalem, His holy mountain, and that God would cause His face to shine upon His desolate sanctuary.

cards.question: Daniel is honest about why he's asking. What does Daniel say his petitions rest on?
At the end of his prayer, Daniel asks God not to delay.

cards.text: "O Lord, listen! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, hear and act!" That's not a polite little prayer, friend. That's a man asking with everything he's got, because God's city and God's people bear His name.
Daniel is still praying, still confessing his own sin and the sin of his people Israel, still bringing his petition about God's holy mountain.

cards.question: While Daniel is still praying, ___ comes to him in swift flight, the man Daniel had seen in the earlier vision.

cards.text: Gabriel arrives about the time of the evening sacrifice, in swift flight. Friend, my oven takes twelve minutes to preheat, and Daniel's visitor shows up while he's still MID-PRAYER.

cards.question: Gabriel tells Daniel why he's come. What is Gabriel here to give Daniel?
Gabriel says an answer to Daniel's prayer went out at the beginning of his petitions.

cards.text: Gabriel also tells Daniel he is highly precious, and the last thing anybody called me in that junk drawer was "what IS this thing?" Then comes the message: seventy weeks are decreed for Daniel's people and his holy city.

cards.question: Seventy weeks are decreed for Daniel's people and holy city. What does Gabriel say they are decreed to do?

answers.text: Bring down the king of Persia
Send the people back to Egypt

cards.text: And there's more on that list: stop their transgression, make atonement for iniquity, bring in everlasting righteousness, seal up vision and prophecy, and anoint the Most Holy Place.

cards.question: Gabriel gives a starting point: the decree to restore and rebuild Jerusalem. Counting from there, who does Gabriel count up to?

cards.text: From the decree until the Messiah, the Prince, Gabriel says there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. And Jerusalem will be rebuilt, with streets and a trench.

cards.question: Gabriel says Jerusalem will be rebuilt in peaceful and easy times.
After the sixty-two weeks, Gabriel says something hard is coming for the Messiah. What will happen?

answers.text: He will be cut off and have nothing
He will rule from the city of Babylon
He will be crowned in the citadel of Susa

cards.question: Gabriel says the people of the prince who is to come will destroy the city and the sanctuary.

cards.text: The end will come like a flood, and until the end there will be war, with desolations decreed. Then Gabriel says he will confirm a covenant with many for one week.

cards.question: Gabriel says he will confirm a covenant with many for one week. In the middle of that week, what will he put an end to?

cards.text: Gabriel's last words: "And on the wing of the temple will come the abomination that causes desolation, until the decreed destruction is poured out upon him." That's where his message ends, friend, and it's a heavy one.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 6 quotes "what IS this thing?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says Daniel is 'one of God's people living far from Jerusalem.' Daniel 9:1-2 doesn't say this, so it is an outside fact with no reference. The card also cites only Daniel 9:1-2, which doesn't cover it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats card 3's answer (sackcloth and ashes) and adds a joke. It cites Daniel 9:3 again and tells nothing new from the passage.

rule.text:
Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
- No recap cards.

findings.problem: The joke mixes the two images. Daniel 'raises his hand' inside the everyday work-meeting picture, so the comparison and the Bible setting become one image.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't share the core action. The fact is someone arriving quickly while Daniel is still praying. An oven taking twelve minutes to preheat is about warming up, not arriving. The card also mostly repeats card 2 ('while he's still MID-PRAYER'). The only new detail is the evening sacrifice.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The joke makes up a new moment from the junk drawer, where someone called him 'what IS this thing?' That moment isn't in his backstory. Jokes may only make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The question says 'something hard is coming for the Messiah.' Both wrong answers are good outcomes (ruling from Babylon, being crowned in Susa), so the setup rules them out and gives away the right answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Then Gabriel says he will confirm a covenant with many for one week' reads as if Gabriel himself will confirm the covenant. The text leaves 'he' unnamed, and it is not Gabriel speaking about himself. Quoting the BSB ('And he will confirm a covenant with many for one week') would keep it open without pointing to Gabriel.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The question has the same problem: 'Gabriel says he will confirm a covenant... what will he put an end to?' reads as Gabriel being the one who acts. The question needs to give its own context, for example by quoting the BSB line, so the baker isn't left with a 'he' that seems to mean Gabriel.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Many story cards are plain retellings with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice: stop 1 cards 5, 9, 11, 13 and 17, and stop 2 cards 1, 8, 10 and 14. Across the walkthrough there are only a few real laughs.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
